key_insight: A noisy 36-qubit trapped-ion processor can still recover meaningful spin excitation spectra and magnetic correlations of Cs2CoCl4 when circuit compression and error mitigation are combined.
engineering_relevance: This work shows that carefully compressed quantum circuits can turn near-term quantum hardware into a practical tool for quantum spectroscopy of strongly correlated materials.
method: Use an ancilla-free local kick protocol to probe spin dynamics.
Compress ground-state preparation and time evolution with classical tensor networks.
Reconstruct dynamical structure factors and nearest-neighbor spin correlations with error mitigation.
evidence_signal: The reconstructed spectra agree closely with DMRG and neutron-scattering benchmarks, with Pearson correlation and structural similarity above 0.9 and normalized mean squared error below 0.15.
watch_item: The approach depends on strong classical compression and mitigation, so its accuracy and scalability may degrade as the target system or circuit depth increases.
paper_title: Quantum simulation of field-tunable spin spectroscopy of the quantum magnet Cs2CoCl4 on a trapped-ion quantum computer
